channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Enhances Control Over KazMunayGas Foreign Assets
item.description: Kazakhstan has included six foreign subsidiaries of KazMunayGas (KMG) in a list of strategically important economic sectors subject to state property monitoring. Among these is KMG International, which manages oil refineries in Europe. The decree, signed by Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov, takes effect on October 30.

item.title: Uzbekistan Investigates Reports of Mass Citizen Data Leak
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has launched an investigation into reports of a potential leak of citizens' personal data circulating on social media and Telegram. The probe, involving the State Security Service's Cybersecurity Center and AUTODOC company, aims to verify the authenticity and origin of the data.

item.title: Former National Security Committee Officer's 12-Year Sentence Overturned
item.description: A court has overturned the 12-year prison sentence of Manat Sarbasov, former deputy head of the Shymkent Department of the National Security Committee. He was accused of accepting a 70 million tenge bribe to provide patronage for a private school. The cassation court cited procedural violations in the original trial.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov Arrives in Turkey for Working Visit
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov arrived in Ankara, Turkey, on October 29 for a working visit. He was met at the Etimesgut International Airport by Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz and other officials. Japarov is scheduled to attend the 13th Summit of Heads of State of the Organization of Turkic States.

item.title: Yandex Maps Navigation Now Offers Fuel-Efficient Route Options in Uzbekistan
item.description: Yandex Maps navigation in Uzbekistan has introduced a new feature that calculates fuel-efficient routes. The service now compares available options and suggests the most economical one, alongside the fastest route. This feature aims to help drivers save on fuel by optimizing for smoother, more consistent driving, reducing fuel consumption and environmental impact.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prioritizes Long-Term Infrastructure Development Over Short-Term Gains
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has outlined a long-term vision focusing on infrastructure development, allocating approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by 2029 for schools, hospitals, cultural and sports facilities, and road and utility network upgrades. This strategic investment prioritizes sustainable development and future societal benefits over immediate populist measures.

item.title: Age Limit Imposed on Labor Migrants Departing Tajikistan
item.description: Tajikistan has introduced an age restriction for citizens leaving the country for work. This measure aims to regulate labor migration and potentially protect younger workers. Further details on the specific age range and implementation are expected.

item.title: Uzbekistan Pursues Strategic Priorities at Organization of Turkic States Summit in Ankara
item.description: Uzbekistan is set to advance its strategic priorities at the upcoming Organization of Turkic States (OTS) summit in Ankara on October 29-30. The summit marks the fifth anniversary of the organization's transformation into a full international body, emphasizing trade, transport, and investment cooperation. Uzbekistan has proposed over 85 initiatives since joining.

item.title: Uzbekistan and US Collaborate to Combat Transnational Crime and Terrorism Financing
item.description: Uzbekistan and the United States are joining forces to combat transnational crime, including terrorism financing and human trafficking. A meeting between US Homeland Security Investigations and Uzbek Prosecutor General's Office officials discussed enhancing mechanisms for crime prevention and detection. Presentations covered crypto-asset financing of terrorism and migration issues.

item.title: Tajikistan suspends business inspections for SMEs until 2029, excluding tax checks
item.description: Tajikistan has extended a moratorium on most inspections of small and medium-sized businesses until January 1, 2029. President Emomali Rahmon signed the decree, aiming to alleviate pressure on entrepreneurs. However, tax authorities will still be permitted to conduct inspections.

item.title: Swiss energy group MET Group with €28.6 billion revenue enters Kazakhstan market
item.description: Swiss energy group MET Group, which reported €28.6 billion in revenue for 2025, has registered a legal entity in Kazakhstan. The new company plans to operate in the oil and gas sector, engage in wholesale fuel trading, and manage stakes in local enterprises.

item.title: Two Individuals Detained in Almaty Metro Carrying Weapons
item.description: Two individuals were detained in the Almaty metro at the "Bauyrzhan Momyshuly" and "Zhibek Zholy" stations after knuckle dusters were found on them. Criminal cases have been initiated against both individuals. Police stated that the circumstances are being investigated and legal assessments will be made. Knuckle dusters are considered cold weapons in Kazakhstan and their illegal circulation is prohibited.

item.title: Almaty Scientists and University Leaders Discuss President's Address on National Priorities
item.description: Scientists and university leaders in Almaty discussed the key directions of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address, "Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era." The meeting focused on training specialists for the new economy, developing science, implementing artificial intelligence, and universities' role in solving urban issues. Participants explored ways to implement priorities in higher education and adapt to labor market demands.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Hungary Launch Digital Groundwater Monitoring Project
item.description: Uzbekistan and Hungary are implementing a digital groundwater monitoring project in the Fergana Valley. Namangan State Technical University and Hungarian company GeoGold Kárpátia signed a contract for research and development worth $1 million. The project, a result of a 2025 memorandum, aims to deploy 245 digital mini-stations over five years.

item.title: Relatives of Soldiers Who Died in Caspian Sea Meet with Defense Minister
item.description: Relatives of soldiers who died or were severely injured while serving in the military met with Kazakhstan's Defense Minister Aidoss Mirzakhmetov. The meeting addressed concerns following the deaths of 14 servicemen during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea due to severe weather. The minister assured that each case would be individually reviewed.

item.title: Fitch Assigns 'BB-' Credit Rating to Jizzakh Region of Uzbekistan
item.description: Fitch Ratings has assigned a 'BB-' credit rating with a 'Stable' outlook to Uzbekistan's Jizzakh region. The rating reflects the region's economic development, financial condition, and creditworthiness, with economic growth rates exceeding the national average. Information on new projects and export potential was also presented.

item.title: UN Rapporteur Warns Against Legitimizing Taliban Without Rights Improvements
item.description: UN Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett cautioned that international engagement with the Taliban must not grant legitimacy without verified human rights progress. He highlighted entrenched repression and discrimination in Afghanistan, urging the international community not to normalize Taliban rule while fundamental rights, especially for women and girls, are restricted.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Support Rural Entrepreneurs in Online Sales Through Marketplaces
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to support rural entrepreneurs by enabling them to sell goods through online marketplaces. The Ministry of Digital Development aims to make digital economy opportunities accessible to rural residents. Initiatives include integrating rural businesses into existing marketplaces, developing delivery networks, and providing training on e-commerce and AI tools.

item.title: Darhan Satybaldy Orders Increased Oversight of Almaty Infrastructure Projects
item.description: Darhan Satybaldy has instructed that oversight of infrastructure projects in Almaty be strengthened. The directive aims to ensure the effective implementation and monitoring of ongoing development initiatives within the city.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Pension Savings Yield 766 Billion Tenge in Investment Income
item.description: Kazakhstan's mandatory and voluntary pension contributions have generated 766.32 billion tenge in investment income since the beginning of 2026. Employer contributions added another 139.39 billion tenge. Since the consolidation of pension assets in 2014, total investment income has reached 14.3 trillion tenge, accounting for about 40% of total savings.

item.title: Bishkek Leads in Traffic Accidents; 572 Deaths in Kyrgyzstan Over Nine Months
item.description: Kyrgyzstan registered 3,624 traffic accidents from January to September, resulting in 572 fatalities, including 88 children. While the number of accidents decreased by 1.4 times compared to the same period in 2025, Bishkek accounted for 27.4% of all incidents. Child injuries remain a concern, with 1,015 accidents involving minors.

item.title: Tansar Islamic Bank Not Licensed by ARRFR, but Approved by AFSA
item.description: Tansar Islamic Bank, established by shareholders of the Tansar financial group, has not applied for a banking license from Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARRFR). However, the bank has received approval from the Astana International Financial Centre's (AIFC) Financial Services Regulatory Authority (AFSA) and is in the process of obtaining its license.

item.title: Canadian Company to Invest $24.7 Million in Kazakhstan Gold-Copper Mine
item.description: Canadian firm Mogotes Metals plans to expand its operations in Kazakhstan by developing the Beskauga gold-copper-silver project in the Pavlodar region. The company intends to pay up to $24.7 million for the right to fully acquire the deposit. A holding company was registered in October 2026, with payments scheduled through February 2029. An initial payment of $2.5 million is planned.

item.title: Kazakhstan Defense Minister Pledges Action on Military Deaths and Injuries
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Minister Aidarbekov met with families of soldiers who died or were severely injured during service. He promised to personally review each case and study the provided materials. The meeting also included the chief military prosecutor and National Guard representatives. This follows the ministry's announcement of a military reform, including the creation of independent military consultant institutes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's SMEs Contributed 50.9% to GDP in 2025, Report Shows
item.description: Small and medium-sized businesses accounted for 50.9% of Kyrgyzstan's GDP in 2025, according to preliminary data from the National Statistical Committee. The sector's share averaged 42.7% over the 2021-2025 period. In 2025, 26,000 small and 1,200 medium enterprises employed 138,800 people. Foreign direct investment in SMEs totaled $276.5 million, a 30.5% decrease from 2024.

item.title: Budget Chinese Tires May Disappear from Kazakhstan Market Due to New EAEU Regulations
item.description: The Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) may ban the sale of tires that do not meet new requirements regarding carcinogenic substances. Russia's initiative will be discussed by the EAEU Council in November 2026. If approved, the decision could reduce the availability of inexpensive tires in Kazakhstan by summer 2027.

item.title: Economists Analyze Most Beneficial Mortgage Programs for Kazakhstan's Citizens
item.description: Kazakhstan does not have a universal mortgage program beneficial for all citizens. Economists advise considering personal income, savings, housing needs, and loan repayment when choosing a mortgage. Programs like '7-20-25' and 'Otbasy Bank' offer specific benefits, while commercial banks have higher interest rates.

item.title: US Dollar Trades at 453.60 Tenge on Kazakhstan Stock Exchange
item.description: The national currency strengthened by 3.33 tenge. The weighted average exchange rate of the US dollar at the close of trading on Thursday on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange decreased to 453.60 tenge.

item.title: Bishkek Mayor Questions Officials Receiving 'Lunch Money' from Businesses
item.description: Bishkek Mayor Aybek Dzhunushaliyev has ordered an investigation after a municipal employee received 5,000 soms (approx. $60) from a businessman labeled 'for lunch.' The mayor expressed outrage, questioning officials' integrity and demanding accountability for potential corruption, stating that even ten or a hundred officials could be detained if necessary.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Accountability for Road Contractors and Technical Supervision
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to enhance accountability for contractors and technical supervisors involved in road construction and repair quality. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov instructed the Ministry of Transport to strengthen control over local road networks. Measures will be developed to hold organizations responsible for construction and repair quality.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Arrives in Ankara for Working Visit
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan has arrived in Ankara, Turkey, for a working visit at the invitation of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. The Uzbek leader is scheduled to participate in the upcoming summit of the Organization of Turkic States.

item.title: Tashkent May Experience Increased Air Pollution for Another 10 Days Due to Inversion
item.description: Uzbekistan's Hydrometeorological Service warns that an atmospheric inversion in Tashkent could persist for another 10 days, leading to increased air pollution. Without wind or rain, pollutants accumulate, exacerbated by the inversion trapping them. Measures are being taken to improve air quality.

item.title: Pakistan and Taliban Face Deepening Rift Amidst Afghan Crisis
item.description: Experts suggest the growing tensions between Pakistan and the Taliban signal a deep rift, not a temporary dispute. Factors include Afghanistan's crisis, the Taliban's legitimacy issues, ties to al-Qaeda, and security disagreements. However, some caution that these differences may be tactical, given Pakistan's long-term strategic investment in the Taliban.

item.title: UNODC Reports Nearly Fivefold Increase in Afghanistan's Opium Production
item.description: Opium production in Afghanistan has surged nearly fivefold in 2026 compared to the previous year, according to a UNODC report. Poppy cultivation increased by 330%, with production rising approximately 400%. Farmers' poverty and lack of alternatives hinder reduction efforts, necessitating international cooperation for livelihood opportunities.

item.title: Taliban Intelligence Arrests Former Afghan Police Commander in Kabul
item.description: Sources in Kabul report that General Allah Dad Fadai, a former police commander under Afghanistan's previous government, has been arrested by Taliban intelligence. Fadai, who previously served in several provinces and returned to Afghanistan about a year ago, is now being held in an unknown location. His arrest highlights ongoing risks for former security personnel.

item.title: UN expert warns against normalizing Taliban's repression in Afghanistan
item.description: A UN special rapporteur has warned the international community not to normalize the Taliban's entrenched system of repression and discrimination in Afghanistan. Richard Bennett stated that five years after the Taliban's return to power, they show no sign of retreating from systematic human rights violations, instead intensifying their crackdown, particularly on women and girls.

item.title: Turkmenistan residents face heating issues amid energy export wealth
item.description: Residents in Turkmenistan, a country rich in energy resources and exports, are reportedly experiencing significant heating problems in their homes. Despite the official start of the heating season, many areas, including Turkmenabat, have not received adequate heating. Citizens are resorting to gas stoves for warmth, while also facing warnings against their misuse and being charged for non-existent heating services.

item.title: Dr. Nakamura's Legacy Highlights Urgent Need for Agricultural Transformation in Afghanistan
item.description: Dr. Tetsu Nakamura, a physician who worked in Afghanistan, recognized that hunger and lack of water were root causes of suffering. He advocated for sustainable food production through restoring irrigation, not just temporary aid. His work in Nangarhar demonstrated that simple water management could transform lives, raising the question of why agriculture hasn't been a central economic pillar.

item.title: Central Asia May Face Increased Electricity Shortages; Renewables Planned
item.description: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) predicts potential electricity shortages in Central Asia. To address this, plans are in place to launch over 35 gigawatts of solar and wind power capacity in the region by 2035. This initiative aims to bolster energy supply and meet growing demand.

item.title: Manas performers and military to feature at Ala-Too Square event in Bishkek
item.description: Bishkek's central Ala-Too Square will host a republican event on October 30th, celebrating the epic "Manas" and Kyrgyz cultural heritage. The program includes military cadets, National Guard soldiers, law enforcement, Manas performers, and improvising akyns. The event aims to promote national traditions and patriotism among youth.
